newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish bourse head calls for more transparency.
newsitem.headline: Spanish bourse head calls for more transparency.

text.p: Spanish listed companies should be more transparent and responsible in order to attract investors, National Stock Market Commission (CNMV) chairman Juan Fernandez Armesto said on Tuesday.
He called for better regulation and management of listed companies.
"We must be extraordinarily demanding (in order to attract investors)," Armesto told journalists.
"We need a unity of vigilance, systematically revising deal by deal in order to develop a system of control of illicit operations," he added.
He called for more independent advisers to company boards and recommended that companies followed "a code of good government to achieve transparency of decisions as well as sticking to rules."
The CNMV is to introduce greater policing of bourse transactions from February, he added.
Spanish daily El Mundo reported on Tuesday that the CNMV had created a special team of five or six people that would be dedicated to spotting stock market irregularities from February onwards.
Referring to electricity firm Endesa whose case is pending, he said the decision might take up to a year to emerge.
The CNMV said it would start proceedings against Endesa, its chairman and finance director for a "very serious infraction" of bourse regulations.
Endesa denies that it violated CNMV rules during its bid for 75 percent of regional utilities Fecsa and Sevillana de Electricidad in October.
